calls.head: Hofer’s rough record against the Sharks is a coincidence
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Hofer has been shaky against the Sharks, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Expect the usual Hofer.
calls.call: If Hofer starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .914 than to his .877 against the Sharks.
calls.nums: 6 starts against San Jose: .877 save percentage · .914 against everyone else
calls.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against San Jose, 2,689 shots against everyone else
calls.happened: J. Hofer stopped 24 of 27 shots (.889), against his usual .914 and his .877 against this team before tonight.

calls.head: The Blues should get some good looks
calls.body: The Blues make their shots count, and the Sharks are near the bottom of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Blues to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Blues’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
calls.nums: St. Louis 6th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · San Jose 23rd for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: St. Louis’s average shot had a 10.1% chance of going in, against their usual 6.7%.
calls.beyond: St. Louis’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 10.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

calls.head: Don’t blink and you still might miss the shots
calls.body: San Jose plays some of the league’s slowest games, and so does St. Louis. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than 78.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, slower than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): San Jose 29th (78.4), St. Louis 28th (78.5)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 76.7 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the slower team’s usual 78.4 and a league average of 81.7.

STL.head: We gave St. Louis a 62% chance, but San Jose had other ideas.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose a 38% chance, and San Jose proved us wrong.

surprises.head: San Jose won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, St. Louis wins 73. San Jose won anyway.

surprises.head: San Jose leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: San Jose’s bottom-six forwards played 46% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Nedeljkovic steals one in St. Louis
paras: Connor McMichael opened the scoring early in the first. Twice the Sharks answered a Blues lead. Darnell Nurse won it 1:03 into overtime.
The Blues had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Blues win about seven in ten. Alex Nedeljkovic made the difference in net, stopping 24 of 26.

items.text: The Blues haven’t won in three.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
